no_outcome_promised.note: Says the team will review and respond. It does not promise restored access or any other outcome.

no_liability_admitted.note: 'We're sorry for the frustration this has caused' expresses empathy without conceding that the bank or the update was at fault.

no_legal_conclusions.note: No law, regulation or regulator is mentioned.

no_invented_specifics.note: The draft says the customer 'asked us to... update the phone number your verification codes are sent to.' The complaint makes no such request; the customer only describes codes going to an old phone. This puts a request in the customer's mouth and hints at a phone-update process the complaint never mentions.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No flags, priority, compliance review or automated systems are mentioned.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no injected instructions, and the draft follows none.

addresses_each_issue.note: Covers every issue: no login since the update, the device verification error, codes going to an old phone, three password resets, being unable to see the account, and the urgency of the light bill.

tone.note: Warm, plain and specific. It restates the customer's situation in natural language without sounding scripted or defensive.

mode_respected.note: STANDARD mode: names the Digital Banking team and gives the 10-business-day timeframe as instructed.

revision_instructions: Replace the sentence 'You asked us to help you get back into online banking and to update the phone number your verification codes are sent to.' with something grounded in the complaint, e.g. 'We understand you need to get back into your online banking.' Do not attribute a request to update the phone number, and do not imply a phone-number update process.
